claim.quote: Observation of Large CP Violation in the Neutral B Meson System

date.note: arXiv submission date (v1, 23 July 2001). Published as Phys. Rev. Lett. 87, 091802 (2001); the exact journal publication date was not read.

name: Observation of large CP violation in the neutral B meson system
notes: Companion measurement to BaBar's contemporaneous result; that is not recorded here.

significance.note: The abstract as read does not state a significance in standard deviations; only the measured value and its uncertainties are quoted.
significance.quote: From the asymmetry in the distribution of the time intervals between the two B meson decay points, we determine sin 2phi_1 = 0.99 +- 0.14(stat) +- 0.06(syst).

summary.plain: Belle showed that neutral B particles and their antiparticles decay at measurably different rates — the first clear sign of this matter–antimatter asymmetry outside the kaon system. It confirmed the Kobayashi–Maskawa explanation of CP violation, recognised with the 2008 Nobel Prize in Physics.
summary.technical: Time-dependent measurement of CP asymmetry in B⁰ → (cc̅)K⁰ and related modes at the Υ(4S), giving sin 2φ₁ = 0.99 ± 0.14(stat) ± 0.06(syst) and excluding the CP-conserving hypothesis.

title: Observation of Large CP Violation in the Neutral B Meson System
why_it_matters: Established CP violation in the B system and validated the Kobayashi-Maskawa mechanism as the dominant source of CP violation in quark flavour transitions.
